newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of FOMC.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's first leg of a two-day meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy setting body.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet on February 4 and 5 to discuss the future of the country's monetary policy. The Fed is expected to announce the results on Wednesday.
The market is also waiting for tonight's release of the U.S. December new home sales and leading indicators data.
New home sales for December are forecast to be around 745,000 units compared with 772,000 units reported in November.
December leading indicators are expected to be unchanged from November's 0.1 percent gain.

"Rates were steady to a little bit softer in the morning on some position adjustments. Everyone is waiting for fresh clues to market direction from the results of tonight's FOMC meeting although most people are not expecting any change in interest rates. The new homes sales and leading indicators figures due later today will probably be overshadowed by the FOMC meeting," a local dealer said.
"The next key economic indicator will be Friday's January employment report," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed were unchanged from Monday's common 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, four-months eased 1/16 point to 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, six-months eased 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 and twelve-months was unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent.
